info.title: LLM-IDE API
info.description:
Multi-user, self-hostable backend for the LLM-IDE conversation-driven
project system.  Every state-mutating endpoint requires a JWT access
token; data is scoped per user (tenant) at the SQL layer.

DELETE /agent/v2/session.summary: Drop a chat's SDK-session mapping (chat deletion)
DELETE /agent/v2/session.description: Removes the chat→SDK-session mapping row and best-effort deletes the SDK transcript files recorded for the session id (per-user engine home).

responses.200: Mapping dropped (sdkSessionId is null when none was recorded)

DELETE /kb/agent/personas/{id}.summary: Delete a persona by ID (refuses if it is the last one)

DELETE /kb/agent/project-memory.summary: Remove one captured fact, or clear a repo's captured facts

responses.404: Repo not on the caller's allow-list

DELETE /kb/agent/session-memory.summary: Delete everything session memory captured for one chat session
DELETE /kb/agent/session-memory.description: Called when the user clears or deletes a chat, so its captured memory does not outlive it. A real DB delete (kb/session-memory.mjs, table `session_memory`) — distinct from project memory (`/kb/agent/project-memory`, above), which is durable and never touched by a session's lifecycle, only its own explicit per-fact edit/delete. Not repo-scoped, so no allow-list resolution is involved.

DELETE /kb/agent/tool-approvals.summary: Revoke one rule, one legacy grant, or everything
DELETE /kb/agent/tool-approvals.description: Revocation only ever removes permission — the tool simply asks again — so there is nothing to gate. Returns the remaining set so a caller re-renders from the server's own view.

responses.200: The remaining rules and grants, and how many were removed

DELETE /kb/chat/sessions/{id}.summary: Delete a chat session and its messages

DELETE /kb/chat/sessions/{id}/messages.summary: Clear a session's messages, keeping the session

responses.404: feature_disabled — LLMIDE_FEATURES omits gantt_issues; the route module is not loaded

GET /auth/google/callback.description: Google redirects the user's browser here after consent — there is no Authorization header on this request, so it is public (allow- listed in server/auth.mjs PUBLIC_PATHS). The `state` query param (minted by POST /auth/google/start) carries the userId and PKCE verifier; the handler exchanges `code` for tokens, stores the refresh token in the vault, and always returns an HTML page (never throws) so the tab can close itself.

GET /auth/google/status.description: Only the user who initiated the flow (via /auth/google/start) may read its status.

responses.200: Current status of the sign-in flow
responses.403: State belongs to a different user

GET /kb/activity.summary: List the authenticated user's activity feed

parameters.query.since: Return only items with id > this value (incremental poll cursor)
parameters.query.limit: Maximum number of items to return. Clamped to 1-200; the default is 100 when absent or zero.

GET /kb/agent-sdk.summary: The backend's Claude Agent SDK version against the npm registry's latest

responses.200: `running` is what this process loaded at startup, `installed` what is on disk (they differ after an update until the backend restarts — `restartNeeded`). `canUpdate` is false while remote access is on.

GET /kb/agent/catalog.summary: Executable skills + plugin subagents for the Code Assistant "/" menu

responses.200: Catalog of skills the agent can actually dispatch

GET /kb/agent/commands.summary: Slash-commands enabled for this user (powers the chat "/" autocomplete)

GET /kb/agent/feedback/stats.summary: Aggregate agent feedback statistics for the user

GET /kb/agent/generation-library.summary: Doc Gen / Visual template and command catalog from the enabled skills sources
GET /kb/agent/generation-library.description: The kit's `templates/` and `commands/` families for the Mac app's Doc Gen and Visual menus. Each entry carries its `surface` (doc | visual), which divides the two menus. First enabled source wins on an id collision. Added in API v51.

GET /kb/agent/persona.summary: Get the user's active agent persona (legacy single-persona surface)

GET /kb/agent/personas.summary: List all agent personas and indicate the active one

GET /kb/agent/project-memory.summary: Auto-captured chat-memory facts for a repo (project-memory viewer)
GET /kb/agent/project-memory.description: Send the client's indexedRepos candidate paths; the server resolves the FIRST allow-listed one — the same target memory capture writes to — and returns its absolute root so subsequent DELETEs address the same file. A repo that is not on the caller's allow-list yields `{ facts: [], repo: null }` without touching disk.

parameters.query.repo: Candidate repo path; repeatable, tried in order.
parameters.query.workspaceRoot: Open Explorer folder, tried after the repo candidates.

GET /kb/agent/runs.summary: List sessions that currently have the agent attached

GET /kb/agent/skill-library.summary: Central skills-repo discovery catalog (skills the agent cannot execute)
GET /kb/agent/skill-library.description: The `skills/` + `runtime/` families NOT already in /kb/agent/catalog. The client attaches a chosen skill's SKILL.md to the next request as context.

GET /kb/agent/tool-approvals.description: Claude-style rules made from the approval card's "always allow" button: per user, per project (the resolved workspace root), per tool, and for shell tools per command PREFIX (`npm test`, `git status`). A compound command never matches a prefix rule. A rule only ever skips the interactive approval a `prompt`-tier call would park; it can never promote a `blocked` command or a write outside the workspace, because those checks run first and unconditionally. `approvals` are the pre-v55 global per-tool grants: no longer honoured by either engine, still listed so they can be seen and revoked.

GET /kb/chat/sessions.summary: List unified chat sessions (shared by macOS + extension)

GET /kb/chat/sessions/{id}.summary: Fetch one chat session with its messages

parameters.query.limit: Max messages returned. The default is 50, with a minimum of 1 and a cap of 200.

GET /kb/entity/{id}.summary: Fetch a single KB entity (action / decision / blocker / etc.) by ID

GET /kb/export-all.summary: Export every KB row for the caller as newline-delimited JSON, paged by cursor

GET /kb/issue-schedule.summary: List the user's scheduling overlay for a repo's issues (gantt parity)
GET /kb/issue-schedule.description: GitHub issues carry no start/due/estimate/dependency fields. This per-user overlay supplies them so the Mac gantt can draw real bars. Keyed by (provider, repo, issueNumber); user_id-scoped.

responses.404: feature_disabled — LLMIDE_FEATURES omits gantt_issues; the route module is not loaded

GET /kb/issues.summary: List issues from the connected tracker for a repo (read-only)

GET /kb/live/sessions.summary: List active in-memory live capture sessions for the user

GET /kb/live/{id}.summary: Poll for new captions since a sequence number

parameters.query.since: Return captions with sequence > this value

GET /kb/live/{id}/stream.summary: Server-sent events stream of a live capture session's captions
GET /kb/live/{id}/stream.description: Content-Type text/event-stream. At most MAX_SSE_PER_USER concurrent streams per user (429 TOO_MANY_STREAMS beyond that).

responses.200: SSE stream of caption events for the session
responses.429: Too many concurrent live streams for this user

GET /kb/meeting/{id}.summary: Fetch a single meeting record by ID

parameters.query.include: Opt-in extras. `transcript` adds the stored transcript text as `transcript`.

GET /kb/outcomes/stats.summary: Aggregate outcome statistics for the user (counts by state)

GET /kb/outcomes/task/{id}.summary: List all outcome records for a specific plan task

GET /kb/plan/{id}.summary: Fetch a single plan by ID

GET /kb/plans.summary: List plans for the authenticated user

parameters.path.id: 1–128 chars of alphanumerics / `_` / `-` (rejected otherwise, so a crafted id cannot traverse).

GET /kb/review/get/{id}.summary: Fetch a single review item by ID

GET /kb/review/list.summary: List review items (optionally filtered by status)

GET /kb/routing-tiers.summary: The caller's tier routing config plus per-tier usability (API v67+)
GET /kb/routing-tiers.description: The stored config and, for each tier, whether the server can run it right now — the same check the server's resolver applies (custom provider registered/enabled/keyed; DeepSeek keyed; OpenAI/Google keyed or, API v68+, their CLI installed for the logged-in subscription path; v69+: the CLI must pass a `--version` health probe, which this request may wait a few seconds for) — and whether it can run on the Agent SDK engine (first-party Anthropic, or a custom provider with an Anthropic-compatible endpoint and a key). The Mac app uses it to skip a route the server would refuse.

GET /kb/slack/conversations.summary: List Slack conversations visible to the saved token
GET /kb/slack/conversations.description: `complete: false` means pagination was cut short (a `slack_conversations_incomplete` warning is logged); the returned channels are still usable.

GET /kb/stats.summary: Per-user KB statistics (meeting count, entity counts, etc.)

GET /kb/system/status.summary: Unified system status — KB stats, active captures, agent runs, pending reviews, outcome summary

GET /kb/usage/limits.summary: Read the user's per-model usage caps (built-in chains merged with overrides)

GET /kb/usage/ratelimits.summary: Latest provider API rate-limit snapshot (API-key mode only; null otherwise)

responses.200: Rate-limit buckets (requests/tokens limit, remaining, reset) or null

GET /kb/usage/resolve.summary: Which model in a provider's chain should run next (auto-fallback)

parameters.query.prefer: Preferred model — kept when healthy, stepped down only when constrained

responses.200: Resolution (model, status ok|degraded|paused|unconfigured, resetAt, reason, engaged)

GET /kb/usage/summary.summary: Live per-model usage + resolved active model per provider (dashboard)

GET /kb/usage/turn-composition.summary: The caller's newest v2 chat turns, with the measured context split (migrations 0040/0044)

responses.200: Newest first. Token fields are approximate (chars / 4) for LLM-IDE text and the SDK's own estimates for sdk* fields; null when not measured.

POST /agent-sdk/spike.summary: P0 spike — direct Claude Agent SDK query over SSE (temporary)
POST /agent-sdk/spike.description: Proof-of-concept surface from the P0 spike (SDK streaming, kb_search MCP tool, vault-key auth). Temporary by design; its successor is the /agent/v2/* protocol above.

POST /agent/v2/cancel.summary: Stop the caller's in-flight Agent-engine turn for one chat
POST /agent/v2/cancel.description: Same abort a dropped stream triggers (SDK subprocess and parked decisions). The chat's turn lock is released once the turn finishes unwinding (about two seconds), so a client retries its send after this rather than at once. Scoped to the calling user. Server API v54.

responses.200: Answered; `cancelled` says whether a turn was running

POST /agent/v2/decision.summary: Answer a parked approval (AskUserQuestion or ToolApproval) from a v2 stream
POST /agent/v2/decision.description: Tenancy-checked: the deciding user must own the session the approval was parked under; foreign decisions are 403 and logged. An AskUserQuestion is answered with `answers`; a ToolApproval with `action`. A ToolApproval's approval_request carries an optional `suggestion` { toolName, pattern?, scope: project|session, label } — what `always-allow` would save: a project command-prefix / tool rule, or (edits) a grant for this chat.

responses.200: Decision delivered; the stream emits approval_resolved and the turn continues
responses.403: DECISION_FORBIDDEN — belongs to another user or session

POST /agent/v2/stream.summary: Run one Agent-SDK chat turn and stream its events over SSE
POST /agent/v2/stream.description: The server owns the chat→SDK-session mapping: consecutive turns with the same `agentContext.chatSessionId` resume the same SDK conversation. `fresh: true` deliberately skips the recorded id (client asked to start over, e.g. after a SESSION_UNRESUMABLE error). Validation errors answer as plain JSON before the SSE headers are written; once streaming, failures arrive as a terminal `data: {"type":"error",...}` event instead of an HTTP status.

responses.200: SSE stream of engine events — init first, mode_set right after init, result or error last. Event types: init, delta, tool_use_start, tool_args_delta, tool_result, usage, approval_request, approval_resolved, mode_set, result, error, sdk. Unknown event types and fields must be ignored by clients.

POST /auth/google/start.description: Persists the caller's own Google OAuth "Desktop app" client credentials to the vault, mints a PKCE pair + one-time state token, and returns the Google consent URL for the client to open in a browser.

POST /auth/logout.summary: Revoke current refresh token (or all sessions with allDevices=true)

POST /auth/me/secrets.summary: Set or delete an encrypted secret

POST /chat.summary: Chat with the meeting assistant about a transcript

POST /code-assist.summary: Code-assist chat with optional file attachments
POST /code-assist.description: With `Accept: text/event-stream` the answer streams as SSE events (`progress`, `chunk`, `done`, `tasks`, `error`). A turn that fails because the named provider cannot run (missing / disabled / keyless, or its CLI is missing, broken or logged out) before ANY progress or chunk event went out sends `{ type: 'error', error, code: 'PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE' }` (API v70+) — the buffered path's 400 with the same code — so a client can retry once without its tier route. Every other error event has no `code`.

responses.400: Validation error, or (API v67+) PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE — the named provider is missing, disabled or has no API key; message is the Settings hint

POST /code-assist/decision.summary: Answer a parked act-tool approval from a legacy /code-assist stream
POST /code-assist/decision.description: The legacy-engine counterpart of POST /agent/v2/decision, backed by the same in-process decision registry. A 'prompt'-tier run-bash command parks an approval and emits a progress event of phase `approval_request`; this route resolves it. Tenancy-checked: the deciding user AND the session the approval was parked under (the legacy chat's `agentContext.sessionId`) must both match, or the answer is 403.

responses.200: Decision delivered; the parked tool call resumes (or is denied) and the stream continues
responses.403: DECISION_FORBIDDEN — belongs to another user or session

POST /extract-entities.summary: Extract structured actions, decisions, and blockers from a transcript

POST /generate-doc.summary: Generate a structured Markdown document from a template and/or a command, over source content

POST /generate-docx.summary: Generate a DOCX meeting-notes file from a transcript

responses.500: AI parse or DOCX build failure

POST /generate-notes.summary: Generate markdown meeting notes from a transcript

responses.200: Notes generated (JSON or SSE depending on Accept header)

POST /generate-questions.summary: Generate targeted follow-up questions from a transcript

POST /kb/activity.summary: Record an in-process activity event (Mac app)

POST /kb/agent-sdk/update.summary: Install the registry's latest Claude Agent SDK in this backend's checkout
POST /kb/agent-sdk/update.description: Runs `npm install @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@<latest> --save-exact`, then loads the new package in a separate process; if either fails the previous version is reinstalled. Never restarts the backend — the client does. One update at a time; refused while a chat turn is running, and /agent/v2/stream answers 503 SDK_UPDATING while it runs; refused while remote access is on unless LLMIDE_ALLOW_SDK_UPDATE=1.

POST /kb/agent/ask.summary: Free-text Q&A with the meeting agent (uses active persona voice)

POST /kb/agent/dispatch.summary: Attach the meeting agent question-loop to an active live session

POST /kb/agent/feedback.summary: Record user feedback on an agent question (useful / noise / later)

POST /kb/agent/stop.summary: Detach the meeting agent from a live session

POST /kb/analyze-risks.summary: Re-compute LLM risk assessment for a plan

POST /kb/box/test.summary: Verify Box credentials and folder access

POST /kb/chat/sessions/{id}/messages.summary: Append a message to a chat session

POST /kb/code-sync.summary: Annotate plan tasks with matching code file references from the KB

POST /kb/conflict-questions.summary: Surface cross-meeting conflicts and undecided items from KB history vs current transcript

POST /kb/connect-box.summary: Index a Box folder's documents into the KB

POST /kb/connect-git.summary: Index a local Git repo's code files into the KB

POST /kb/connect-github-issues.summary: Fetch and index GitHub issues for a repo

POST /kb/connect-qa.summary: Index JUnit XML test results into the KB

POST /kb/connect-tickets-json.summary: Index an inline JSON array of tickets (Backlog, Jira, or generic)

POST /kb/custom-providers.summary: Sync the Mac app's custom model providers to the server
POST /kb/custom-providers.description: Replaces the CALLER's custom-provider list (other users are untouched). The list is persisted per user, so it survives a server restart; an empty array deletes it. Entries without an id, a name, or an http(s) baseURL are dropped.

POST /kb/delete.summary: Delete a meeting and its associated entities

POST /kb/dispatch.summary: Preview / send tasks to GitHub, Backlog, or Linear

responses.409: Conflict. Code REVIEW_CONFIG_MISMATCH (API v75+) when the request `config` names a destination (e.g. repo) different from the approved review; credentials in `config` are still accepted

POST /kb/email/classify.summary: Classify a fetched email with LLM and extract to-dos (60 s server timeout)

POST /kb/email/fetch.summary: Fetch recent emails via IMAP and return them for ingestion

responses.200: Fetched messages (server-side high-water mark and dedup applied)
responses.400: Missing host/user or no IMAP password stored

POST /kb/email/seen.summary: Record imported message IDs and advance the IMAP high-water mark

POST /kb/email/test.summary: Test IMAP connection using stored app password

responses.400: Missing credentials or no password stored

POST /kb/generate-code.summary: LLM-generate files + tests for a single task (preview only)

POST /kb/generate-plan.summary: Synthesize a plan from a meeting (chains analyze-risks + code-sync by default)

POST /kb/ingest.summary: Upsert a meeting and replace its entities

POST /kb/ingest-code-graph.summary: Store a repo's structural code graph (nodes/edges) for agent traversal
POST /kb/ingest-code-graph.description: Written by the macOS app after each knowledge-graph generation. Populates `code_graph_nodes`/`code_graph_edges` with `source='structure'`, which backs `findRelatedSymbols` and the code-sync agent's symbol grounding. Large graphs arrive in batches — set `replace` on the first batch only, otherwise each batch discards the previous one. One request accepts at most 5000 nodes and 20000 edges.

responses.200: Stored counts for this batch, plus entries dropped as malformed
responses.400: Missing fields or batch over the per-request cap
responses.404: feature_disabled — LLMIDE_FEATURES omits code_graph_3d; the route module is not loaded

POST /kb/ingest-scip.summary: Ingest a SCIP index into the code-graph tables
POST /kb/ingest-scip.description: `repoPath` must be on the caller's repo allow-list (compared after `path.resolve`), since it is used as the graph's identity key.

responses.400: Missing args or SCIP index failed
responses.403: Repo path not on the allow-list

POST /kb/live/{id}/append.summary: Append caption chunks to an active live session

POST /kb/live/{id}/finalize.summary: Finalize a live capture session (marks it done; ingest separately via /kb/ingest)

POST /kb/loop/agent-run.summary: Run one headless, confined agent step for the Mac Loop
POST /kb/loop/agent-run.description: The Loop's skill stages, stage repairs and fault repairs. Runs on the Claude Agent SDK with FILE TOOLS ONLY (Read, Glob, Grep, Edit, Write) plus one read-only code-graph search, `mcp__llmide__find-code`, served in-process (strict MCP config: no user, project or plugin MCP server can join), working directory `repoRoot`, and every path confined to it (symlinks resolved; secret paths such as `.env` and `.git/` refused). No shell, no network, no plugins, no operator settings. A step that repeats itself or keeps failing is stopped as `no_progress`. Nothing is ever parked for approval: a refused tool call is denied and listed in `denied`. `repoRoot` must be absolute and either at or below a root on the caller's repo allow-list (`/auth/me/repos`) or a linked git worktree of one under a `.llmide-loop-worktrees/` or `loop-worktrees/` directory. `extraRoots` (at most 4) widens the confinement to a project's notes directory in the split layout: each must be an existing directory named `llm-doc` whose parent contains `system/project.json` and is `repoRoot` itself or an ancestor of it at most 3 levels up (symlinks resolved); anything else is 400 `EXTRA_ROOT_NOT_ALLOWED`. Grep and Glob patterns naming a secret path are refused, and every Grep carries the secret denylist as negative globs. A run cut off by the timeout or a disconnect is still metered for the usage the SDK reported. When any requested skill id is not installed the agent does not run (`ran: false`, the id in `unresolvedSkills`). `timeoutMs` (default 30 min, clamped to 1 s – 4 h) aborts the run; a client disconnect aborts it too. Rate-limited on the `agentTurn` bucket. `provider` (v66, the Mac's Loop tier route) runs the step on an Anthropic-compatible custom provider through its Anthropic base URL and key (the same gateway contract as `/agent/v2/stream`); the tools and confinement are identical for every provider, and the run is metered under the provider that ran. Absent means first-party Anthropic. Server API v58 (provider: v66).

responses.200: The run finished (or did not start because a skill is missing — see `ran`)
responses.400: VALIDATION_FAILED, REPO_ROOT_NOT_ALLOWED — repoRoot outside the allow-list, EXTRA_ROOT_NOT_ALLOWED — an extraRoots entry is not the project's llm-doc, PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE — the custom provider is missing, disabled or keyless, or PROVIDER_NOT_AGENT_CAPABLE — the provider has no Anthropic-compatible endpoint
responses.404: feature_disabled — LLMIDE_FEATURES omits auto_tasks; the route module is not loaded

POST /kb/mcp-connector/classify.summary: Classify one ingested connector item and extract to-dos
POST /kb/mcp-connector/classify.description: Accepts the Source Connector manifest engine's fixed `{ body: { …fields } }` envelope; the connector id rides inside the field map as `connectorId`.

responses.502: The model did not return valid JSON

POST /kb/mcp-connector/fetch.summary: Fetch new items from a remote MCP connector (server-side dedup against the seen ledger)

responses.200: Items not yet imported. Partial success — one unreadable parent is reported in `failures`, not as an error.
responses.400: Unknown connector id, not connected (MCP_UNAUTHORIZED), or no fetch mapping (MCP_NOT_FETCHABLE)

POST /kb/mcp-connector/seen.summary: Mark MCP connector item ids as imported (per user, per connector)

POST /kb/mcp-connector/test.summary: Verify a remote MCP connector's saved OAuth tokens (connect + tools/list)

responses.200: Connected — server identity and available tools

POST /kb/notify/slack.summary: Send a plan / dispatch / custom message via Slack incoming webhook

responses.400: Missing kind, no webhook configured, or notify failed

POST /kb/outcomes/refresh.summary: Poll dispatched tasks across providers and record outcomes

POST /kb/outcomes/retry-failed.summary: Retry all failed dispatched tasks across providers

POST /kb/plan-task/update.summary: Patch a single plan task (status, owner, due, risk, etc.)

POST /kb/plan/delete.summary: Delete a plan and its tasks

POST /kb/plan/save.summary: Create or update a plan without an LLM call (manual / auto-stub)

POST /kb/project/install-skills.summary: Install the central skills kit into a project folder
POST /kb/project/install-skills.description: Used by New Project / Rebuild. The target must already contain `system/project.json`, so an arbitrary path cannot be written to.

POST /kb/providers/models.summary: Fetch the current chat model list for a provider

responses.200: Model ID list (empty when nothing could be listed). For `anthropic` the list comes from the Agent SDK — the account's own models, with or without an API key — in the SDK's order (its default first), with display names in `entries`; if the SDK cannot answer it falls back to the key-based `/v1/models` listing. Other providers: sorted ids from their models endpoint.

POST /kb/providers/verify.summary: Verify an LLM provider credential (live probe or CLI binary check)

POST /kb/review/approve.summary: Execute an approved review item (re-runs guardrails)

responses.200: executed. API v75+: review payloads in all /kb/review/* responses are redacted (token/apiKey/secret/password leaves removed)
responses.409: REVIEW_NOT_PENDING, or REVIEW_RACE when another request claimed the item
responses.422: GUARDRAILS_FAILED at approval time (auto-rejects the item), or CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED (API v75+) when the only failing check is the missing credential: the item stays pending so the approve can be retried with `config`/`pr` credentials or after saving one to the vault

POST /kb/review/delete.summary: Delete a review item from the queue

POST /kb/review/submit.summary: Submit an artifact (dispatch / codegen-apply) for human review

POST /kb/routing-tiers.summary: Sync the Mac app's per-role tier routing config to the server
POST /kb/routing-tiers.description: Replaces the CALLER's tier routing config (other users are untouched), persisted per user. Each tier names a provider + model; each feature names a tier. Every entry is optional and invalid entries are dropped (unknown tier/feature names, a provider outside anthropic|openai|google|deepseek|jev|custom:<id>, a model id outside `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/-]{0,127}(\[1m\])?$`) and reported back in `dropped` (API v67+). An unset or unusable tier (custom provider missing/disabled/keyless, DeepSeek without an API key, OpenAI/Google with neither an API key nor their logged-in CLI — codex/gemini, API v68+; v67 required the key) keeps the role on its default provider and model. API v73+: `jev` (decision-only, key required) is a valid tier provider but serves ONLY the `decisions` feature; any other feature on a jev tier keeps its default.

responses.400: Body is not a JSON object

POST /kb/slack/fetch.summary: Fetch new messages from a Slack channel (incremental, past the per-channel high-water mark)

responses.200: New messages plus a skipped count
responses.400: Validation error or no token saved

POST /kb/slack/seen.summary: Mark Slack messages seen and advance the per-channel high-water mark

POST /kb/slack/test.summary: Verify the saved Slack bot token (auth.test); no request body

POST /kb/summarize.summary: Summarize a transcript with LLM (3-minute server timeout)

POST /kb/usage/record.summary: Record one usage event (used by the Mac Auto Tasks CLI path)

PUT /kb/agent/persona.summary: Set or reset the active agent persona

PUT /kb/agent/personas/active.summary: Set the active persona by ID

responses.200: Updated personas list with new active

PUT /kb/issue-schedule.summary: Create or replace one issue's schedule overlay

responses.404: feature_disabled — LLMIDE_FEATURES omits gantt_issues; the route module is not loaded

PUT /kb/usage/limits.summary: Replace the per-model caps for the providers present in the body

components.FeatureDisabled: 404 body for a path owned by a feature the server was started without (LLMIDE_FEATURES). Deliberately not the Error envelope: a client can tell it from an unknown route without parsing a message.
